newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks drift lower in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks drift lower in morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks drifted lower in Thursday morning trade, taking a breather after a futures-related rally lifted the Hang Seng index 213 points on Wednesday.
"It's a mixed market after index (futures) expiration. That is out of the way and that is why the market has turned quiet," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
October Hang Seng index futures expired on Wednesday.
The Hang Seng index was down 9.12 points at 12,396.35. Turnover was HK$1.69 billion after the first hour of trade.
November Hang Seng futures were down 32 points to 12,416.
Analysts said with fresh economic data expected out of the United States on Thursday and Friday, investors were likely to take a cautious stance for the rest of the week.
Among the data, September U.S. personal income and consumption data are due on Thursday and the October U.S. jobs report on Friday.
"I would say we will be just trading sideways waiting for news out of the States," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities. "There is a real basket of economic data."

Mak agreed. "It will probably hold at this level. There are more important figures coming out of the U.S. so people will keep an eye on these figures for an indication on where interest rates will go and also keep an eye on the U.S. election," he said.
The U.S. presidential election will be held on November 5.
Mobile telephone operator SmarTone Telecommunications Holdings made its market debut on Thursday. The stock opened at HK$17.25, unchanged from its issue price, but then slipped to HK$16.90.

Shares in Whimsy Entertainment rose HK$0.14 to HK$1.93. The company said it had agreed to issue 28 million new shares at HK$1.50 a share to a substantial shareholder, raising net proceeds of about HK$41 million for general working capital.
Among the blue chips, Cheung Kong moved higher despite market weakness, advancing HK$0.50 to HK$61.50. New World Development also made gains, adding HK$0.20 to HK$44.50.
Hang Seng Bank was off HK$0.50 at HK$91.25 and HSBC Holdings held steady at HK$156.50.
